claims: Satoshi Nakamoto is the pseudonymous creator(s) of Bitcoin.
Satoshi Nakamoto published the original whitepaper in 2008.
Satoshi Nakamoto launched the network in 2009.
Satoshi Nakamoto's true identity remains unknown.
A 2026 investigation published by Fortune pointed to British cryptographer Adam Back as a likely candidate for Satoshi Nakamoto.
The 2026 investigation published by Fortune aligns with a New York Times report.
Adam Back is a British cryptographer.
Satoshi Nakamoto vanished in April 2011.
Satoshi Nakamoto stepped back from the project.
Satoshi Nakamoto is believed to hold approximately 1.1 million Bitcoins.
Satoshi Nakamoto's approximately 1.1 million Bitcoins have never been moved.
Satoshi Nakamoto's approximately 1.1 million Bitcoins are worth over $125 billion.
Proposed candidates for Satoshi Nakamoto's identity include Hal Finney, Nick Szabo, and Adam Back.
According to Wikipedia, no one has been definitively proven to be Satoshi Nakamoto.
A detailed investigation was led by journalist John Carreyrou.
John Carreyrou suggested that Adam Back, the CEO of Blockstream, is Satoshi Nakamoto.
Adam Back is the CEO of Blockstream.
John Carreyrou's investigation cited linguistic analysis showing similar nonstandard hyphenation errors in early emails and forum posts.
Adam Back’s early work was on Hashcash.
Hashcash is the proof-of-work system used by Bitcoin.
A New York Times investigation reported a decrease in Adam Back's online activity during the period Satoshi Nakamoto was active.
Adam Back has denied being the creator.
